name: Anger Regulation
description: Support for understanding, expressing, and regulating anger in healthy and constructive ways.

immediateActions.title: 60-Second Cool Down
instructions: As soon as you notice anger rising, say silently to yourself: I am feeling angry and I have space to choose my response
Step back physically if possible: take one step away or turn slightly
Take a fast, deep inhale through the nose for 2 counts, then exhale slowly through pursed lips for 6 counts
Repeat the breath pattern 3 more times
Ask yourself: On a scale of 1-10, how hot is my anger right now? Name it aloud if safe
Ask: What do I actually need right now? Space? A drink? To say nothing for 2 minutes?

immediateActions.title: Physical Release Sequence
instructions: Go somewhere private if possible
Clench your fists as tightly as you can for 5 full seconds, then release completely and shake out your hands
Tense all the muscles in your face, hold for 5, then release and sigh out loud
Push both hands against a wall as hard as you safely can for 5 seconds, then release
March or jog in place vigorously for 30 seconds, then stop and stand still
Take 3 slow breaths in and out and notice the shift in energy

immediateActions.title: Anger Unpacking: What Is Underneath?
instructions: Write the event that triggered your anger in one or two sentences
Rate the anger from 1 to 10
Ask: Under the anger, am I also feeling hurt? Unheard? Disappointed? Afraid? Overwhelmed? Disrespected?
Circle any secondary feelings that are also present
Ask: What is it that I wanted or needed in this situation that I did not get?
Write down one thing you want to say or do next, and one thing you want to avoid saying or doing

immediateActions.title: Constructive Expression Prompt
instructions: Decide what the actual issue is, separate from the person involved
Write one sentence using the I-statement format: I feel [emotion] when [specific situation/action] because [effect on you]
Write down one specific request of what you would like instead, framed positively
Choose a good time to speak: not when either of you is hungry, tired, or still heated
Deliver your I-statement calmly and state your request clearly
Listen to the response without interrupting; you do not have to agree, just to hear

safetyGuidance: Anger is a natural human emotion that signals something matters to us; the goal is not to eliminate it, but to express it in ways that do not harm yourself or others. If anger feels out of control, frequent, or is damaging your relationships, consider working with a therapist who can help you develop personalised regulation skills. Everyone deserves support in this area.
